page.layout: One printed page with a running head and page number at the top; one text column of full lines; a partial fragment of the facing left page visible at the far left edge as margin remnants (not transcribed as notes); catchword-style signature line at the foot: "B" at left and "Mos" at right of the last line of the column.

main_text.p: tura rerum cogitatione, velut navi, qua per mare Philosophicum feratur, oblata, cursum dirigit non ad Cyno- suram Rationis, sed ad Erraticam Eventus, longiusque provehitur, & gratulatur sibi, quamdiu obvia con- sentiunt, & institutum errorem, nec remorantur, nec produnt; donec quasi tempestate aliquâ, ad inopinatam & votis non respondentem Experien- tiam, tamquam ad saxum adhære- scat, is profectò in hac Erronum clas- se, familiam ducit, & prætoriam quasi navim gubernat; Cæteri lint- ribus ac phaselis passim insecuti, dum numero inter se ac turbâ confidunt, consuescunt cum erroribus, solitos eos ac familiares reddunt, & (si opinio- nes præjudicatæ præstare periculum possent) etiam tutos: cum, aut non er- rare penitus, aut non imperitè vi- deantur errare qui tam frequentes er- rant.Breve dicam, Sors parit errores,

page.notes: Left edge shows cropped remnants of the facing page (fragmentary words such as "ascx", "ad", "elle") which are not transcribed. Running head and page number are at the top of the page. The signature letter B and catchword Mos sit on the same line at the foot. Some words in the italic line "is profectò" and "ad inopinatam" were read with moderate confidence.
